ig_carousel_topic.topic: Why your win rate matters less than your ROI
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text: Your Win Rate Is Not the Number That Pays You
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors chase 60%, 65%, even 70% win rates.
The assumption: win more bets, make more money.
That math only works if every bet is the same size at the same price.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
ROI is what actually moves your bankroll.
A bettor going 54% on +120 underdogs beats a bettor going 60% on -145 favorites.
The odds are doing more work than the wins.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example:
100 bets at 60% win rate, all at -145: net -3.0u
100 bets at 54% win rate, all at +120: net +9.6u
Same discipline. Very different outcomes.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
Our YTD: 270-229, 54.1% win rate, +45.4u, 9.3% ROI.
We track ROI first. Win rate is context, not the goal.
